verdict.rationale: For a GPU, the natural documented programmatic interface is NVIDIA's first-party CUDA Toolkit, which provides a runtime library, a compiler, and C++ and Python tile-kernel programming models for driving GPU compute. The evidence does not explicitly tie the toolkit to the RTX 5070 Ti, and it shows no API for controlling device settings. There is also no OpenAPI spec (all probes 404), though an llms.txt exists on the developer portal. Missing for 10: explicit confirmation of RTX 5070 Ti support in the API docs, a documented device-control or management API, and hands-on corroboration of programmatic use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The toolkit includes GPU-accelerated libraries, debugging and optimization tools, a C/C++ compiler, and a runtime library.
cuTile Python is an expression of the CUDA Tile programming model in Python... allows you to write tile kernels in Python.
With it, you can develop, optimize, and deploy your applications on GPU-accelerated embedded systems, desktop workstations, enterprise data centers, cloud-based platforms, and supercomputers.
